source_text: parvulorum nec diabolo coniugia eum genitalium commentor artificem assevero peculium diaboli
pass_a_gloss: Parvulorum nor to-the-devil marriages him genitalium commentor artificem assevero peculium of-the-devil.

lemmas.lexica: LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: Once I begin to show them, they will become more bitter toward you.

Augustine reports Julian accused him of making those people the devil’s property, assigning marriages to the devil, calling the devil the maker of the genitals, the arouser of men, the one who makes women fertile, and the creator of infants.

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
